newsitem.title: UK: Eurobonds see asset-backed bonds and retail bonds.
newsitem.headline: Eurobonds see asset-backed bonds and retail bonds.

text.p: The launch of two asset-backed Eurobonds on Wednesday gave a further boost to this nascent European market, dealers said.
The first Finnish markka-denominated international asset-backed deal was issued by Fennica. The three-tranche deal consisted of fixed- and floating-rate class A notes.
An official at joint lead manager ING Barings said the deal represented another step in the development of the European asset-backed sector.
"It is the first such deal syndicated internationally, and the FRN is the first markka floater too," the official said.
Although the bulk of the paper would be sold to Finnish institutions, there was some outside interest too, he said.
In the mark sector, Salomon Brother lead-managed a 1.25 billion mark seven-year credit card-backed bond for a BankAmerica unit.
The deal will be priced later to yield 34 b.p. over Bunds.
It is the second asset-backed mark security Salomon has brought with a fixed-rate structure.
This broadens the appeal of the asset class as European institutions find it easier to understand than asset-backed floaters, dealers said.
The asset-backed mark sector was opened in April when Citibank launched a 1.0 billion mark three-year FRN.
Elsewhere, bonds targeted at European retail investors provided the bulk of activity.
In dollars DePfa issued a $200 million December 1998 deal at 14 b.p. over Treasuries, which traders said looked very tight.
The EIB 300 million mark December 2001 deal launched at 16 b.p. was subject to similar criticism.
"DePfa is already trading flat to fees, and the EIB is at around 20 b.p over," said a trader at a U.S. bank.
"All these deals are sold to retail, and don't look very good or interesting," he added.
On the brigher side, dealers said Ford Motor Credit's $1.0 billion five-year global bond launched on Tuesday and due for pricing later today had been well-received.
"There was a lot of demand out of the U.S. and European investors have been attracted by this strong bid," said a syndicate manager.
The indicated price range was 48 to 50 b.p. over Treasuries.
